title: DialogHeader owns its controls, in normal flow
decision: The expand and close buttons move into DialogHeader, in normal flow to the right of the title, and pr-20 goes. closeButton, onExpand and expandLabel move from DialogContent to DialogHeader, where they render. Both buttons declare type="button", so D37's paired rule holds inside the shared component once.
context: DialogContent rendered the expand and close buttons as a sibling of its children, inside an absolute top-3 right-3 container. The buttons belonged to no section; DialogHeader carried pr-20, a 5rem right padding that existed only to make room for them; and they came after the children, so close was the dialog's last tabbable element, after every field and the submit button. Once a form boundary wrapped the header, they would also fall outside the form that D37 draws.

alternatives.option: Keep the absolute positioning and draw the form boundary without the header
alternatives.reason: The header would sit on a different level from body and footer, and pr-20 and the tab order would stay as they were. The absolute positioning is what needed fixing.

alternatives.option: Keep the props on DialogContent and pass them to DialogHeader through context
alternatives.reason: Callers would not change, but a prop declared on a component that does not render it is hidden coupling. Only five callers passed these props; moving them explicitly is cheaper.

alternatives.option: Keep DialogHeader as a column and put the controls above the title with self-end
alternatives.reason: The controls would take a whole row above the title and make the header taller. Beside the title, on the same row, is where they belong.

consequences: DialogHeader is one row with two cells, content and controls. The title has real width and no longer avoids something invisible.
Close and expand are in the natural tab order, inside the header, before the body's fields.
The control group is vertically centered on the title's first line with -my-1.5, since the 32px buttons are taller than the 20px title line.
unconfirmed-set-dialog, the one dialog without a DialogHeader, no longer needs closeButton={false}.
game/options/edit's flex-row items-center override on DialogHeader stopped applying; its back button moved into DialogTitle, as in game/new.
revisitTriggers: A dialog needs controls but has no DialogHeader.
An overlay style needs its controls somewhere other than the header.
